tasks.objective: Close the validate-on-read gap: bind each stored record's content so a well-formed edit fails closed on read. In MemoryStore.append, after building the event, extend a SHA-256 hash chain: link_i = sha256(link_{i-1} + "\n" + json.dumps(event, sort_keys=True)), link_0 = "". Keep the chain outside the event (memory_event.schema.json is frozen): for JSONL, a sidecar file next to the log (e.g. events.jsonl.chain, one "<event_id> <link>" line per record); for SQLiteStorage, a new event_chain table created in __init__ with append/list methods. In MemoryStore.events() (and so read_refs), after validate_event, recompute the chain over the records read and raise VerificationError on any mismatch, missing link, or record/link count difference. Test both backends by editing stored records directly.
success_criteria: Records written by MemoryStore.append still read back unchanged on both the JSONL and SQLite backends, including after reopening the store

Editing a stored record to a different but schema-valid value (output.objective to another non-empty string, top-level objective, node_id, or recorded_at) makes events() and read_refs() raise VerificationError on both backends
Deleting a stored record, swapping two records, or deleting the chain sidecar/rows makes events() raise VerificationError
The JSONL log line format is unchanged, so tests/test_runtime_replay_w2t2.py still replays byte-identically
The new test file fails on the starting commit and the full suite passes after the change
constraints: Edit only src/neural_node_swarm/memory.py and src/neural_node_swarm/sqlite_storage.py, plus one new test file such as tests/test_validate_on_read_integrity_w3t1.py; task 2 adds a new module and must not collide with you
Keep MemoryStore(path), MemoryStore(storage=...), id_source, clock, append's return value and the duplicate-ID rejection unchanged; keep validate_event as is
Keep the SQLite events table and SQLiteStorage.append_event/list_events/get_event working for direct callers (tests/test_sqlite_storage.py uses them without MemoryStore)
Deterministic only: no randomness or wall clock in the chain; do not edit any schema file

tasks.objective: Add src/neural_node_swarm/multi_hop_matched_cost.py with run_multi_hop(db_path, memory, *, policy, scenario, generations=6, inject_at=3). Host first commits hand=10, leg=20. Successors run via Orchestrator.run_governed_chain; each reads hand and leg through a read-only reader and records the reads in 3 valid node outputs. The host factory (called once per generation) commits the previous successor's proposal before building the next; only generation inject_at proposes hand=90 (evidence_ref record:hand). Scenarios: clean (no proposal), poisoned (evidence hand=10), corrupted (evidence hand=90). Policies: promotion (PromotionGate over InheritanceStore), gated_shared (shared dict, write applied only if the same evidence-equality check passes), shared (ungated baseline). Return per-generation reads, wrong/correct/abstentions, first_contaminated_generation, evidence_checks used, and a does_not_show list of strings. Add compare(...) running every policy x scenario.
success_criteria: shared/poisoned: hand is wrong in every generation after inject_at and correct before it, so contamination injected several generations deep is measured
promotion and gated_shared use the same evidence_checks count in every scenario (matched cost), and compare() asserts or reports that equality
promotion and gated_shared/poisoned: 0 wrong reads; corrupted: hand wrong in every generation after inject_at for both, first_contaminated_generation = inject_at + 1
Every result reports abstentions and a non-empty does_not_show list (e.g. no model workers, single region injection, equal outcomes are not a general equivalence claim)
Each successor's three rounds are committed to the MemoryStore as valid node outputs, and the new test file fails on the starting commit and passes after
constraints: Only add src/neural_node_swarm/multi_hop_matched_cost.py and one new test file such as tests/test_multi_hop_matched_cost_w3t2.py; do not edit any existing file (task 1 edits memory.py and sqlite_storage.py this wave)
Write memory only through MemoryStore.append via Orchestrator; never write or read the log file directly, since task 1 adds a hash-chain sidecar checked on read
Use only public APIs: Orchestrator.run_governed_chain, PromotionGate, GatedReader, InheritanceStore, MemoryStore(path); do not rely on wall-clock values or uuids in assertions
No live model calls, network or new dependencies
